description: When it comes to gen AI, the habits, attitudes, and ideas of Gen Z are a harbinger of the future of work—and how the rest of us will feel when we get there. A survey of nearly 2,500 U.S. adults between the ages of 18 and 28 years old revealed some surprising findings. Most members of Gen Z use gen AI and, contrary to conventional wisdom, Gen Z’s relationship with these tools is more pragmatic than personal. Moreover, they use it even in situations where they’re explicitly told not to. The survey also revealed anxieties about what gen AI is doing to its users: Respondents worried it’s making people lazier and less intelligent by crowding out opportunities to learn by doing, critical thinking, and social learning. There are, however, some reasons for optimism. Respondents reported that AI tools can offer novel viewpoints, help them break problems into smaller parts, and free up time for meaningful work.
title: How Gen Z Uses Gen AI—and Why It Worries Them
